title: Burglar steals safe, cash from Jersey City eateries - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Johnson ,
5 hours ago
Police in New Jersey are searching for a burglar who was caught on camera breaking into a Jersey City restaurant and stealing a safe and a cash register before targeting a second restaurant next door.
The break-in occurred at Luna Restaurant on Grove Street in Jersey City. According to the restaurant's owner, the thief entered through a bathroom window, stole a safe from an office and then exited by breaking through the front door.
Despite the weight of the safe, the suspect was able to drag it out of the restaurant. The owner said the safe remained locked even after its combination was damaged and estimated it weighed between 50 and 100 pounds.
"He moved fast. He kind of put two and two together. It seems like it wasn't his first rodeo. So he came to this store, or they come to a he came through a window, are actually bathroom window, smashed it and came in that way and then exited by breaking the front door and getting out," said Luna owner Julian Muscio.
Authorities said the suspect then entered More Asian Bistro next door through a small window. Once inside, he rummaged through the kitchen area and took an estimated $200 from the cash register.
A manager at More Asian Bistro, who did not want to be identified on camera, expressed concern that both crimes occurred directly across the street from City Hall.
"Look around. He know everything already. How can he know from the back door? How can you know from the front door? Because Fernando, a city hall. See a lot of camera," the manager said.
Both restaurants were left in disarray following the break-ins. Detectives were at the scene searching for additional evidence.
Muscio said he released surveillance video of the crime to alert other business owners and residents in the area.
"So my goal in releasing the videos to the public was to let my other fellow business owners know, and maybe even homeowners know in the area that, you have to be vigilant," Muscio said. "And today was me. Tomorrow could be you. So take those precautions seriously."
Police have not announced any arrests, and the investigation remains ongoing.
